look_here_first: Look at texture before color: this is an herbaceous perennial with conspicuously silky few-foliolate leaves and a densely white-villous, fuzzy conic-to-cylindrical flower head.

project_inclusion.range_basis: BONAP native county map supported by Travis native record, Williamson County flora, and wild Burnet County occurrence. Purola's introduced Hays planting is excluded.

best_field_traits: herbaceous perennial from woody taproot/root crown
odd-pinnate leaves usually with 3–7 larger silky/strigose leaflets
terminal headlike spike tightly packed and conspicuously fuzzy
bracts, rachis and calyx densely white-villous/sericeous
morphology_keys.habit: Herbaceous perennial; not a woody shrub.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Usually 3–7 obovate to oblanceolate conspicuously silky leaflets.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Dense terminal headlike spike, conic to cylindrical.
morphology_keys.calyx: Bracts, rachis and calyx densely villous/sericeous.
morphology_keys.fruit: One-seeded indehiscent pod retained with the calyx.

comparisons.key_distinctions: D. compacta has narrow linear leaflets and a dense but less uniformly silky head; D. enneandra has a loose elongated spike; D. frutescens is woody with many tiny leaflets.
